title: Wireless Devices and Technologies

header.html: 2.3 Given a scenario, select and configure wireless devices and technologies: channels, channel width, non-overlapping channels, regulatory impacts (802.11h); frequency options (2.4, 5, 6 GHz, band steering); SSID, BSSID, ESSID; network types (mesh, ad hoc, point to point, infrastructure); encryption (WPA2, WPA3); guest networks and captive portals; authentication (PSK vs enterprise); antennas; autonomous vs lightweight access points
the official CompTIA Network+ N10-009 exam objectives, version 4.0

html:
1Frequencies and channels

Band Facts
2.4 GHz Longer range, better wall penetration, slower and crowded; only three non-overlapping channels in the US: 1, 6 and 11 (20 MHz wide)
5 GHz Faster, shorter range, many more non-overlapping channels; DFS channels need radar detection
6 GHz Newest (Wi-Fi 6E and 7), very wide channels, little interference, shortest range, WPA3 required
Channel width Wider (40, 80, 160 MHz) = more speed but fewer free channels and more interference
Band steering The AP or controller pushes dual-band clients to 5 GHz (or 6 GHz)
Regulatory impact Allowed channels and power differ by country; 802.11h adds dynamic frequency selection (DFS) and transmit power control to avoid radar
Exam tip

. Use channels 1, 6 and 11 at 2.4 GHz to avoid channel overlap between neighboring APs.

2SSIDs and network types

Term Meaning
SSID (service set identifier) The network name
BSSID (basic service set identifier) The MAC address of one AP radio
ESSID (extended service set identifier) One SSID shared by several APs for roaming
Network type Meaning
Infrastructure Clients connect through an AP
Ad hoc (IBSS) Clients connect directly, no AP
Mesh APs relay traffic wirelessly to each other
Point to point A wireless bridge between two sites with directional antennas

3Security and access

Item Detail
WPA2 AES-CCMP encryption; PSK (pre-shared key) for homes and small offices
WPA3 Stronger, SAE (Simultaneous Authentication of Equals) replaces PSK exchange, resists offline guessing, forward secrecy
PSK vs Enterprise PSK: one shared passphrase. Enterprise: 802.1X with a RADIUS server, each user has credentials
Guest network Separate SSID and VLAN with internet-only access and often a captive portal
Captive portal A web page shown before access (terms, voucher, login)
Exam tip

. "Each employee signs in with their own credentials" = WPA2 or WPA3 Enterprise (802.1X and RADIUS). "One shared passphrase" = PSK.

4Antennas and AP types

Item Meaning
Omnidirectional antenna Radiates in all horizontal directions; general coverage
Directional antenna Focuses a beam (Yagi, parabolic, patch): longer range, point to point
Autonomous AP Configured and managed on its own
Lightweight AP Managed by a wireless controller (for example over CAPWAP); central policy and roaming
Exam tip

. WPA3 uses SAE; WPA2 Enterprise and WPA3 Enterprise use 802.1X with RADIUS. PSK is one shared passphrase.

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Three neighboring access points at 2.4 GHz must avoid interfering with each other. Which channels should be used?

  • A1, 2 and 3
  • B4, 5 and 6
  • C3, 7 and 9
  • D1, 6 and 11
Show the answer

Answer: D. Channels 1, 6 and 11 do not overlap.

S2A company wants each employee to authenticate with unique credentials on Wi-Fi. Which setup fits?

  • AWPA3 Enterprise with 802.1X and RADIUS
  • BWPA2 with a shared passphrase
  • CAn open network with a captive portal only
  • DMAC filtering alone
Show the answer

Answer: A. Enterprise mode authenticates each user through RADIUS.

S3A guest network should show a terms-of-use page before granting access. What is used?

  • AA captive portal
  • BA native VLAN
  • CBand steering
  • DA directional antenna
Show the answer

Answer: A. Captive portals present a web page before access.

S4Which technology pushes dual-band clients toward the less crowded 5 GHz band?

  • ABand steering
  • BLink aggregation
  • CChannel bonding at 2.4 GHz
  • DPort mirroring
Show the answer

Answer: A. Band steering moves capable clients to 5 GHz.

S5A building-to-building link of 2 kilometers needs a focused wireless beam. Which antenna fits?

  • AAn omnidirectional antenna
  • BAn internal ceiling antenna
  • CA dipole at 2.4 GHz
  • DA directional antenna
Show the answer

Answer: D. Directional antennas focus the signal for long point-to-point links.

S6A company manages 80 access points centrally with shared policy. Which AP type fits?

  • AAutonomous access points
  • BAd hoc clients
  • CLightweight access points with a controller
  • DRepeaters
Show the answer

Answer: C. Lightweight APs are managed by a controller.

5.2 Recall questions

R1What is the BSSID?

Show the answer

The MAC address of an AP radio.

R2Name the three non-overlapping channels at 2.4 GHz.

Show the answer

1, 6 and 11.

R3What does 802.11h add?

Show the answer

DFS and transmit power control to avoid radar.

R4What replaces PSK key exchange in WPA3?

Show the answer

SAE.

R5What is an ESSID?

Show the answer

One SSID shared by several access points.

R6What does a captive portal do?

Show the answer

Shows a web page before network access.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Bands 2.4 GHz (range, 1/6/11), 5 GHz (faster), 6 GHz (newest, WPA3)
Names SSID (name), BSSID (AP MAC), ESSID (many APs)
Types infrastructure, ad hoc, mesh, point to point
Security WPA2 (AES-CCMP), WPA3 (SAE); PSK vs Enterprise (802.1X, RADIUS); guest + captive portal
Hardware omni vs directional antennas; autonomous vs lightweight APs
